Application Materials.content:
For MSc Business Analytics & AI, supporting documents include:
- Current CV (view [CV template](https://ib-programmes.imperial.ac.uk/hubfs/Website-pdfs/CV-Templates/CV-template-for-FTMBA-and-MSc-applicants.docx) for guidance).
- Personal Statement Questions ([see blog for tips on how to write a personal statement](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/blogs/admissions/top-tips-writing-your-personal-statement/)).
- Complete degree transcripts with English translation if necessary ([view international entry requirements](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/apply/postgraduate-taught/entry-requirements/accepted-qualifications/)).
- Contact details of two academic referees or one academic and one professional referee including their company/business email address. We recommend that one should be your current line manager.
- Career planning question, a quantitative experience statement and programming/computer software experience (if applicable).
- GMAT/GRE is not mandatory requirement for any programme, however, it can enhance the strength of your application.
- English language scores (if required i.e. TOEFL, IELTS. [View English language requirements](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/programmes/english-language-requirements/https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/programmes/english-language-requirements/)).
References: You will need to share the contact details of two academic referees or one academic and one professional referee. Please note we cannot accept references sent from personal or free email addresses, such as Gmail, Hotmail, Yahoo etc. Referees will receive a notification upon application submission to provide a reference for the candidate. Each reference letter submitted must be sent from an academic or professional email address; references sent from personal email addresses, such as Gmail, Hotmail, 126, 163, Sina, QQ, and Yahoo, cannot be accepted.
Essays are a vital part of your application. The questions for the MSc Business Analytics & AI programme are:
1. Please discuss your career plans after graduation. (350 words)
2. Why do you want to study at Imperial Business School and how will you contribute to our community? (500 words)
3. Imperial’s values are Respect, Collaboration, Integrity, Innovation, and Excellence. Describe a time where you embodied one, or more, of these values and explain the impact it had. (500 words)
Quantitative experience statement: You should use the quantitative experience statement on the application form to list the most advanced quantitative courses that you have taken in your academic career to date and to provide brief examples of the relevant topics covered by the programme. Alternatively, if you have gained quantitative experience through work experience, please describe this in the quantitative experience statement. In the quantitative experience statement, you need to list up to five of the most quantitative modules or elements of your studies to date. You should detail the main topics of study (eg: algebra, probability etc) and the level of study (eg: high school, undergraduate degree, short course etc).

Interview Requirements.content:
- Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete an online interview, through Imperial's online interview platform. This is the best opportunity to demonstrate your passion and drive, and why you want to study a Master's at Imperial.
- Interviews are conducted through the video interview platform; candidates can access it online to record and submit their answers. The interview process typically takes about **20 minutes** and does not require extensive preparation.
- The interview aims to supplement the written application and help candidates convey their suitability for their chosen Master's by answering questions about previous experience and future aspirations.
- AI/Chat GPT guidance: The purpose of the interview is to get to know more about you. Imperial wants to see how you approach problems, your motivations and wider interests. If malpractice or answers provided are not genuine are identified, this may factor negatively into the admissions committee decision.
- Application decisions will be communicated by the corresponding decision date for the round in which you applied; applicants should refer to the [key dates and deadlines](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/business-analytics/admissions/#dates-deadlines) for timeframes.

Academic Requirements.content:
- You should have a **First or Upper Second Class Honours undergraduate degree** from a recognised university or the [international equivalent](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/programmes/international-entry-requirements) in a quantitative discipline such as Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, or a quantitative economics degree.
- Your quantitative experience should typically include topics such as **advanced calculus, probability, statistics and linear algebra**. Complete the [online Maths test](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/business-analytics-maths-test) to determine if you are suitable to apply for the programme.
- MSc Business Analytics & AI includes modules using programming languages such as **SQL, R, and Python**, so previous experience of using these or an interest in coding and programming will add weight to your application.
- Work experience is **not a requirement**, although undertaking relevant internships and work placements will add weight to your application. The programme typically looks for candidates with **no more than three years of work experience**; those with more than three years will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
- Most MSc programmes require at least an **Upper Second Class Honours degree or international equivalent** to be admitted. Work experience can add weight to an application, but would not replace the academic requirement.
- China applicants: Imperial requires a **Bachelor’s degree awarded with a final overall weighted average mark of at least 85% from a Project 211 university**.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content:
GMAT is not required for MSc Business Analytics & AI, but will add weight to your application. For the [GMAT 10th edition Exam](https://www.gmac.com/gmat-other-assessments/about-the-gmat-exam), you will need scores in the **90th percentile**. Similarly, if you are taking the GRE, you will need scores in the **90th percentile**. Scores are valid for **five years from your appointment date**. GMAT or GRE is highly recommended for candidates with less quantitative degree backgrounds to strengthen their application for this highly competitive programme.
GMAT/GRE is not mandatory requirement for any programme, however, it can enhance the strength of your application.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
All home, EU, and overseas applicants must demonstrate English language proficiency. Students who were not awarded their degree in a qualifying English-speaking country must demonstrate their proficiency by completing an approved English language qualification at the required level. Minimum test requirements for the most popular tests are:
- **IELTS (academic): A minimum score of 7.0 with minimum scores of 6.5 in all elements**
- **TOEFL iBT:** Tests taken before 21 January 2026: **A minimum score of 100 overall with minimum scores of 22 in all elements.** Tests taken after 21 January 2026: **We accept an overall score of 5.0 with minimum scores of 5.0 in all elements.** We will accept both scores for a period of two years.
- **Duolingo English Test: 125 Overall with no less than 115 in any band score**
More detailed information can be found on the [English language requirements page](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/programmes/english-language-requirements).
English language scores should be submitted if required, i.e. TOEFL, IELTS. It is not compulsory to submit the results of an approved English language test with your application, but it is strongly encouraged and will add weight to your application if you are able to show that you have met the language requirement prior to applying.
The Business School does not offer pre-sessional English courses and does not accept attendance of a pre-sessional English course as a means of meeting the English language requirement.

Program Overview.content:
The MSc in Business Analytics & AI equips students with advanced computational, machine learning, and AI capabilities for an increasingly data-driven world. Students develop expertise in predictive, prescriptive and AI-powered decision models while applying these tools to real-world business challenges through workshops, placement opportunities and an optional extended term. The programme builds coding skills in languages such as Python and R and prepares graduates for roles such as business analyst, data scientist or consultant.
The programme is taught within Imperial College London, a world-leading university with STEM roots, and students learn across the South Kensington and White City [campuses](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/programmes/imperial-advantage/london/#campus) in London. It is ranked 4th in Europe and 8th in the world in the QS Business Master’s Rankings 2026 for Business Analytics, and offers 10 elective options.
Programme preparation and core modules provide foundation skills in statistics, machine learning, data visualisation and genAI. Electives allow students to tailor the programme to their interests, with options focused on industries such as finance, energy and healthcare and technical topics such as LLMs and reinforcement learning. In the summer, students apply their knowledge through a practical project, gaining consulting experience, completing a work placement, or conducting a research report. An [optional extended term](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/extended-term/) allows students to extend the programme duration to 16 months for a longer Work Placement and additional credits.
The programme includes online pre-study modules from July to September and a compulsory on-campus induction week in early September at the South Kensington campus. Over the summer term, students complete the Analytics in Business Capstone, choosing either a Consulting Project or Work Placement; students interested in pursuing a PhD may complete an Individual Research Report with a faculty supervisor instead. The Work Placement gives students the opportunity to apply programme material in a challenging business situation, and the Extended Work Placement provides access to additional and longer summer internship opportunities in the UK and worldwide.
The Class of 2026 includes 107 students, 44% female students, and 34 nationalities.
Career support is tailored to individual aspirations and includes career planning, CV advice and mock interviews before the programme, during study, and after graduation. Graduates work across technology, finance, consulting, healthcare, advertising and luxury, with employers including Amazon, Bloomberg, Mastercard, J.P. Morgan, Google, HSBC and Mastercard. Employment outcomes for the Class of 2024: 95% employed within six months, 56% employed in the UK, and 38% employed in finance. [Find out more about career outcomes](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/business-analytics/career-impact/).
The programme is taught by business-focussed academics and data science specialists researching how analytics, data and AI will transform business and society. Faculty use state-of-the-art technology such as the Data Observatory and combine research with practical insights from industry and government networks. Faculty listed for the programme include Gah-Yi Ban, Associate Professor of Analytics and Operations and Academic Director of MSc Business Analytics & AI; Jiahua Wu; Michael Yeomans; Gokhan Yildirim; Fanyin Zheng; Edward Anderson; Martin Haugh; Esma Koca; Zhe Liu; Fintan Nagle; Laure de Preux; Ragvir Sabharwal; Reza Skandari; Kalyan Talluri; and Wolfram Wiesemann.

Curriculum.content:
MSc Business Analytics & AI programme content includes pre-study and Core modules that prepare students with foundation skills in statistics, machine learning, data visualisation and genAI, elective modules focused on industries and technical topics, and a summer practical project to apply knowledge in a real-world setting through consulting experience, a work placement, or a research report.
- The programme has **10 elective options** and includes elective options such as Advanced Machine Learning, Causal Modelling, and Generative AI and Large Language Models.
- Online pre-study modules: **Online | July-September**. Before the start of the programme, students are expected to complete online pre-study modules delivered via Canvas; some are compulsory and others are strongly recommended.
- Induction week: **On campus | Early September, compulsory**. MSc Business Analytics & AI induction is spent at the South Kensington campus in London.
- Core modules: Data Structures and Algorithms; Data Wrangling and Visualisation; Deep Learning and Generative AI; Fundamentals of Database Technologies; Machine Learning; Maths & Statistics Foundations for Analytics; Optimisation and Decision Models; Statistics and Econometrics.
- Electives: Advanced Machine Learning; Causal Modelling for Business Analytics; Data Management and Ethics; Energy Analytics; Financial Analytics; Generative AI and Large Language Models; Healthcare and Medical Analytics; Leadership in analytics; Logistics and Supply-Chain Analytics; Network Analytics; Retail and Marketing Analytics; Text Analysis for Business.
- Over the summer term, students complete the **Analytics in Business Capstone**, choosing either a **Consulting Project** or **Work Placement**.
- Analytics in Business Capstone applies methodological and domain-specific knowledge gathered throughout the Imperial MSc Business Analytics & AI to business case studies.
- Consulting Project: a substantial group-based consulting project undertaken for a real client.
- Work Placement: an opportunity to apply programme material to a challenging business situation in a real-world setting; students must secure their own work placements and submit details to the Programme Team.
- Individual Research Report: offered to students interested in pursuing a PhD; it constitutes a small piece of research over the summer period, supervised by a faculty member, and can be done in place of the Analytics in Business Capstone module.
- Optional extended term: students may extend the programme duration to **16 months** through an [optional extended term](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/extended-term/), allowing a longer Work Placement, additional professional and global experience, and additional credits; it is subject to an additional tuition fee.
- Extended Work Placement: provides additional work placement opportunities, including longer summer internships in the UK and worldwide.
- Global modules are electives with an application process and additional costs. Options listed include Global Business Challenge (Entrepreneurship), Global Business Challenge (Social Impact), and Global Immersion.
- Global Immersion is an optional, one-week trip with visits to companies across industry sectors, plus social and cultural activities.
- The Business School FAQ states that almost all MSc programmes are **12 month, full-time programmes**; the only exception is MSc Strategic Marketing (online, part-time).

Cost of Attendance.content:
Living expenses at university will vary considerably according to your personal circumstances and lifestyle. Imperial provides a rough guide to what you might expect to spend to live in reasonable comfort in London, considering key costs such as accommodation, food and travel. Tuition fees and study materials are not included.
| Cost | Weekly | Monthly | 9 months | 12 months |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accommodation - College-run | £250 | £1084 | £9,753 | N/A |
| Accommodation - Private sector | £257 | £1114 | £10,023 | £13,364 |
| Food | £71 | £307 | £2,764 | £3,686 |
| Travel (zone 1-2) | £27 | £119 | £1,071 | £1,428 |
| Personal and leisure | £69 | £297 | £2,672 | £3,563 |
| **Totals** | **£417 to £424** | **£1,806 to £1,837** | **£16,250 to £16,530** | **£22,041** |
Figures are rounded to the nearest whole number. Next updates will be published in August 2026.
Additional costs: If you need a Tier 4 student visa, you will need sufficient funds to cover your tuition fees and living costs for your first year of study. The estimates above do not include the cost of flights or insurance. International students may need up to **£1,500** for start-up costs such as accommodation deposits and flights.

Financial Aid.content:
Imperial Business School offers significant scholarship funding to talented Master's applicants, including scholarships and bursaries for MSc Business Analytics & AI. Applicants should apply early and submit their application by one of the [two scholarship submission deadlines](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/business-analytics/admissions/#dates-deadlines) for the 2026 Master's intake; scholarships are awarded from the first deadline onwards. Some scholarships require an additional video interview, with details provided in the offer email.
- African Future Leader Award: up to £20,000. Applicants must be residents in one of the 54 African countries as defined by the United Nations and demonstrate an outstanding track record of leadership and/or leadership potential. Candidates who receive an offer for an MSc programme in admission rounds one or two will automatically be considered.
- Black Future Leader Award: up to £20,000. Applicants must self-identify as being from a Black or mixed Black background and demonstrate leadership and/or leadership potential. Candidates receiving an offer in admission rounds one or two can apply; the offer email includes video assessment details.
- Bright Network Scholarship: up to £10,000. Applicants need to be members of the Bright Network. Candidates who receive an offer for an MSc programme in admission rounds one or two will automatically be considered.
- Dean's Impact Scholarship: £25,000. Applicants must provide clear evidence of tangible impact in entrepreneurship, technology and innovation, sustainability, social impact, or leadership. Candidates receiving an offer in admission rounds one or two can apply; scholarships are limited and earlier application is recommended.
- Female Future Leader Award: up to £20,000. Female applicants must demonstrate leadership and/or leadership potential. Candidates receiving an offer in admission rounds one or two can apply.
- Imperial Excellence Bursary: up to £25,000. Applicants must be self-funded students who demonstrate exceptional academic merit and/or potential, and financial need showing inability to otherwise enrol on an MSc programme. Candidates receiving an offer in admission rounds one or two can apply.
- Imperial Excellence Scholarship: up to £15,000. Applicants should have a strong all-round application with an excellent academic background, career potential and personal statement. Candidates who receive an offer for an MSc programme in admission rounds one or two will automatically be considered.
- Imperial Loyalty Bursary: 10% off tuition. Imperial College London students or alumni who submit their application for an MSc programme in admission rounds one or two and receive an offer will automatically receive this award, subject to availability. Alumni must have achieved an undergraduate degree from Imperial College London awarded at a minimum of Upper Second Class Honours or a Master's degree awarded with a minimum of Merit.
- LATAM Future Leader Award: up to £20,000. Applicants must be residents in one of the 21 Latin American countries as defined by the United Nations and demonstrate leadership and/or leadership potential. Candidates who receive an offer for an MSc programme in admission rounds one or two will automatically be considered.
- LGBTQ+ Scholarship: up to £20,000. Applicants should demonstrate a strong track record of promoting diversity and inclusion and a desire to encourage LGBTQ+ participation in business education and champion equality. Candidates receiving an offer in admission rounds one or two can apply.
Other merit or needs-based scholarships may be available: [Imperial College London](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/) offers postgraduate scholarships, [The British Council](https://study-uk.britishcouncil.org/) offers scholarships for international students, and details of [non-Imperial scholarships](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/students/fees-and-funding/postgraduate-funding/scholarships/further-funding-opportunities-/external-awards/) are available online. Further funding options may also be found in The Grants Register, Awards for postgraduate study at Commonwealth Universities, Study Abroad, and on the [Imperial College London website](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/).
If offered an Imperial Business School scholarship and subsequently offered a larger award by Imperial, the larger award supersedes the first and is not additional. Scholarships awarded by Imperial Business School are in the form of a reduction of the tuition fee; if another scholarship pays the full tuition fee directly to Imperial, the student cannot also receive a Business School scholarship.

Multiple Applications.content:
- You can apply for **up to two courses** in an academic year, only one of which can be for Imperial Business School.
- If you are applying for two courses you should submit only one application, listing your course preferences, rather than submitting two separate applications.
- You should list your preferred course as your first choice and your reserve course as your second choice as applications are considered in the order they are submitted; the second choice will only be considered if the first-choice application is unsuccessful.
- You can only apply for **one Master's course** per admissions cycle in Imperial Business School. To be considered, this course must be submitted as your first choice in your application.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
Under exceptional circumstances, you may apply to defer your admission to the next academic year. Deferral requests are based on a change of circumstance that is outside your control and could not have been foreseen, and that will prevent you from taking up your place on the original course start date. Deferral requests are granted or denied at the discretion of academic departments.
To request a deferral, contact the relevant [admissions team](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/apply/contact/) outlining your circumstances and reasons for your request.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
After receiving your offer, you will need to submit documents to satisfy your offer conditions. As part of this process, you must verify your degree award through the online Qualification Check service, using a unique link provided in your offer conditions. You will then be required to pay a **£6,500 deposit** for the programme. The application portal can be used to respond to your offer and review the full details of your conditions.
You will be able to see full details of your offer conditions once your official offer has been confirmed. For visa applicants, CAS numbers will start to be issued from April, but the CAS will appear on My Imperial only after you have met all the conditions of your offer. Imperial notes: “we cannot provide you with a CAS if you have outstanding conditions on your offer.”
The Business School does **not** offer pre-sessional English courses and does **not** accept attendance of a pre-sessional English course as a means of meeting the English language requirement.
